decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core enterprise communications offer, its still-early and uncertain results are likely acceptable relative to aspiration levels, and the firm's expansion and organisational slack justify keeping it for further learning.

The reported adoption for data-centre and financial-hub connectivity indicates performance above a reasonable aspiration level, and it strongly fits the firm's network-and-cloud infrastructure trajectory.

Optical spectrum connectivity builds directly on the firm's owned fibre strengths and strategic move toward high-bandwidth software-defined services, so management would keep it while accumulating more market evidence.

A voice number ordering portal supports the firm's push toward real-time provisioning and service automation, and with available slack there is little reason to drop a product that reinforces the core platform.

Carrier pre-selection telephony looks like a more legacy voice product with weaker fit to the firm's forward-looking integrated infrastructure strategy, so if its early results are not clearly exceeding aspiration levels management would reassign resources elsewhere.

Direct voice network connection remains close to the established enterprise connectivity business and can complement broader managed network services, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it pending clearer underperformance.
